findings.title: No tests for the new contextual logger middleware or the changed log path
findings.description:
The commit adds a new exported middleware, a new `Logger.FromContext` interface method with a real implementation (`pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:48-56`), and rewrites `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` to get its fields from the context. None of this has a test:
- There is no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go` and no `logger_middleware_test.go` in the package.
- The only test touched is the renamed `metrics_middleware_test.go`, which asserts Prometheus metrics only.
- Nothing asserts that `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` reach the context or the "Plugin Request Completed" line.
- Nothing covers the `CreateMiddlewares` ordering that the log line now relies on.

findings.title: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a throwaway logger, so logs written through it cannot be asserted
findings.description: `FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a fresh instance unrelated to the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware` now logs only via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (`logger_middleware.go:58`). A test that injects a `TestLogger` will therefore always see `InfoLogs.Calls == 0`. This mirrors the existing `TestLogger.New` at `fake.go:18-20`, but here it makes the one production caller of `FromContext` untestable with the project's own fake. Returning `f` would keep calls observable.

findings.title: `LoggerMiddleware` silently depends on middleware ordering and a global tracing provider
findings.description:
`logRequest` used to add `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `traceID` itself. It now emits only `status`, `duration`, `eventName`, `time_before_plugin_request` and `error`. Everything else must arrive through the context:
- **Plugin fields:** these appear only if `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` sits ahead of it in the chain. That holds today at `pluginsintegration.go:160-161`.
- **`traceID`:** this appears only because `tracing.ProvideService` registers a global provider (`pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91-97`). Wiring that skips `ProvideService` loses it.

If either condition breaks, the `grafana-data-egress` line loses its identifying fields with no error and no failing test. The old doc comment stating where the middleware must sit in the stack was deleted; neither `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` nor `NewLoggerMiddleware` documents the requirement.

findings.title: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` dereferences `req` without the nil guard its neighbour has
findings.description:
`QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth` and `CollectMetrics` read `req.PluginContext` unconditionally (lines 40, 45, 50, 55). `LoggerMiddleware`, directly behind it, guards every one of those with `if req == nil` (`logger_middleware.go:63, 77, 90, 104`). Placing the new middleware in front makes those guards unreachable, and a nil request panics here.

The impact is limited in the production chain: `TracingMiddleware` (`tracing_middleware.go:85`) and `MetricsMiddleware` (`metrics_middleware.go:146`) already dereference `req` earlier, as before this change. The real exposure is when this exported middleware is composed on its own or in tests.

findings.title: Fallback branch in `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` is unreachable and would drop context if hit
findings.description: `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` returns either `cl.New(args...)` or `cl` (`pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217`), both `*log.ConcreteLogger`. The `!ok` branch therefore cannot execute today. If it ever did, `d.New()` would return a logger without the contextual attributes and with no signal; falling back to `d` or logging the mismatch would be safer.

findings.title: Naming and comment drift left over from the rename
findings.description:
- The test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` in `metrics_middleware_test.go`.
- The constructor variable is still `imw` (`metrics_middleware.go:77`).
- The helper in the contextual logger file is still called `instrumentContext` (`contextual_logger_middleware.go:27`).
- The `FromContext` doc comment in `pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go` is copied from `New`; it does not say that attributes come from a `context.Context` via the registered contextual log providers.

findings.title: Rename and interface change are complete
findings.description:
- No references to `NewInstrumentationMiddleware` or `InstrumentationMiddleware` remain, apart from the test name noted above.
- The only two implementers of the plugins `Logger` interface under `pkg/` (`grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger`) both gained `FromContext`.
- The `interface{}` → `any` change is purely cosmetic.
- Contextual attributes are still attached regardless of `PluginLogBackendRequests`, as before.
- The logger name `plugin.instrumentation` is unchanged, so existing log filters keep working.
